text:
Brayden Point left a Nov 8 game in Winnipeg after less than six minutes, landed on injured reserve, and came back on Nov 17 like nothing happened: an assist in each of his first two games, both Tampa Bay wins. He has 18 points in 19 games, and 13 of them are assists.

The goals are the part that lags. He has five on 7.5 expected, which is why our numbers flag him as due. He keeps getting to the looks; goals tend to follow chances, and a two-time Cup winner who led the playoffs in goals both springs has earned the benefit of the doubt.

His legs are the tell. NHL Edge has him at 100 bursts over 20 mph, 99th percentile among forwards, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 67% of his entries last season. Carry-ins led to a scoring chance 25% of the time, dump-ins 8%.

What to watch: whether the finishing catches up with the playmaking now that he's healthy. At 3.02 points per 60 he's already producing above our talent range's middle, so the goals are the upside.
headline: Point is back, and the chances never left
